items.title: OpenPost Combines Social Media Scheduling, Content Creation, and Automation in One Self-Hosted App
items.summary: Managing multiple social media accounts can quickly turn into a collection of browser tabs, scheduling tools, and editing applications. Writing a post is usually the easy part. Getting it formatted correctly, creating the accompanying media, and publishing it across different platforms takes considerably more effort. OpenPost is an open-source social media management platform that brings these tasks together. It combines post scheduling, image and video editing, analytics, and automation into a single workspace that you can run on your own server.

items.title: Haven: A Self-Hosted Discord Alternative for Private Communities
items.summary: Discord has become the default gathering place for gaming communities, friend groups, and even development teams. It's convenient, but it also means your conversations, files, and community history live on infrastructure you don't control. For those of us who prefer running our own services, having a similar experience without relying on a third-party platform sounds pretty appealing. Discord-Style Chat on Your Own Server Haven is an open-source, self-hosted communication platform that brings text messaging, voice chat, video calls, and screen sharing together in a familiar interface.

Peoria’s Real Time Crime Center found the car on its cameras. Staff watched it run traffic signals, drive into oncoming lanes and nearly hit several vehicles, and passed that information to officers, police said.

items.summary: A hit-and-run crash in Glendale set off a pursuit that ended with a driver flipping his vehicle onto its side and being taken into custody in Peoria. On Tuesday morning, a real-time crime center received a call from Glendale police alerting them to a hit-and-run crash near 99th Avenue and Northern avenues. items.title: RimWorld meets Dungeon Keeper in the new release of Malignus
items.summary: Malignus is an Early Access dungeon colony sim where you play the dungeon itself, that blends elements of RimWorld and Dungeon Keeper together. A 2D dungeon colony sim and emergent story generator. Play as a boss monster and their underling minions, expand your underground dominion, build traps, and defend your prisoners and treasures from invading adventurers. It released just recently and their current plan is to have about one year of monthly updates, which leads to the full 1.0 release.

items.title: Pinscope – A web-based remote access and vulnerability tracking solution for ESP32, Zephyr, Pico 2 W, and Linux SBCs
items.summary: Pinscope is a remote-access service for microcontroller-class devices like ESP32, ESP8266, Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W, and other MCUs running Zephyr, as well as Raspberry Pi/Linux single board computers. The web-based solution features live logs, metrics, and crash reports, supports OTA updates that stop and roll back in case of failure, and tracks CRA security vulnerabilities for all supported platforms. Pinscope highlights: Web UI – The HTTP server already running on the device gets an HTTPS address of its own.

items.title: Lawmakers Question FAA’s Nationwide AI Rollout
items.summary: A group of 24 House Democrats sent a letter Tuesday questioning the FAA’s decision to expand its artificial intelligence-supported air traffic management system nationwide. Led by House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Ranking Member Rick Larsen, D-Wash., the lawmakers requested documentation of the system’s safety validation ahead of its nationwide deployment on Nov. 10. Safety and Oversight “We have yet to receive any substantive information proving the system was properly validated before its nationwide expansion,” the lawmakers wrote.

items.title: FAA Tightens Line Up And Wait Requirements
items.summary: New FAA staffing requirements for air traffic control towers took effect Tuesday, mandating that a dedicated operations supervisor or controller-in-charge be on duty whenever line up and wait (LUAW) procedures are in use. Mandatory Supervision Under an FAA notice issued in October, the agency amended FAA Order JO 7210.3, which governs air traffic facility operations and administration. Previous guidance recommended against combining supervisory positions with other tower positions during LUAW operations.

items.title: FAA Restores Touch-and-Goes at Centennial Airport
items.summary: The FAA has approved new departure procedures at Centennial Airport (KAPA) near Denver, allowing for the resumption of simultaneous parallel runway departures and touch-and-go operations following seven weeks of restrictions that disrupted flight training at the airport. New Departure Procedures Under the procedures, which took effect Nov. 20, air traffic controllers will instruct aircraft departing from parallel runways to turn 10 degrees away from their respective runway centerlines, establishing a 20-degree divergence between departure paths.

If you don't mind using legacy 802.11 b/g WiFi, there is a newly endorsed driver option…

items.title: FAA Forecasts More Than 52,000 Flights Tuesday
items.summary: The FAA expects more than 52,000 flights across the country Tuesday, marking the busiest day of a nine-day Thanksgiving travel period. According to FAA data, the agency anticipates 417,775 flights operating under instrument flight rules between Nov. 23 and Dec. 1, up 2.2% from last year and 7.5% from 2019. Air Traffic Preparations The increased traffic comes less than two weeks after a nationwide ground stop prompted by communications problems at FAA air traffic control facilities. On Monday, a separate controller shortage temporarily halted flights bound for Chicago O’Hare International Airport.

items.title: openSUSE’s Agama 26 to Support Fully Automated AI-Driven Linux Installations
items.summary: The developers behind Agama, openSUSE’s next-generation Linux installer and successor to the traditional YaST-based system, have announced plans to integrate AI agent support into the upcoming Agama 26 release. The integration relies on a built-in MCP server that gives external AI assistants a structured interface to configure, perform, and monitor operating system installations. For example, users could ask an AI assistant to install openSUSE Tumbleweed with GNOME, configure an NVMe drive with Btrfs, and create a user account without manually going through the installer’s configuration screens.

items.title: Ubuntu details plans to replace its app grid with an AI smart launcher
items.summary: Canonical has shared more detail on plans for an AI-powered Ubuntu launcher, which it hopes will offer users “a new way to interact” with the desktop. In a post on Ubuntu Discourse, Canonical desktop engineer Didier Roche says the goal is to create a unified ‘entry point’ that lets users open apps and find files, but also access AI features when they explicitly want it. This will go beyond providing an alternative to the app grid, allowing for ‘prompt’ style workflows that use privacy-friendly AI models that run locally.

items.title: Terraria devs make significant progress in their quest to conquer the world: crossplay "Phase One"
items.summary: "The crossplay era for Terraria starts here," declares developer Re-Logic in a new Steam post announcing "Phase One" of the iconic sandbox adventure game's crossplay rollout. Terraria's new-fangled crossplay, which allows players on different platforms to share multiplayer worlds and progress, comes with a few caveats, but it's a big step forward nonetheless. "Starting today, for most people using the same Wi-Fi/wired network you will be able to play together with any device which has v1.4.6 Terraria, without a multiplayer subscription," Re-Logic explains.

items.title: Linux 7.4 Disables LLVM Profi Usage To Avoid Performance Hit, Pathological Build Times
items.summary: A change merged this week to the Linux 7.4 kernel and also set to be back-ported to stable kernel branches is to disable use of LLVM's Profi flow-based profile inference algorithm when leveraging AutoFDO. LLVM's Profi is a flow-based profile inference algorithm designed to address inaccuracies and other issues during profile guided optimizations (PGO) by the compiler. Profi has been in use by default since Clang 21 when the "-fprofile-sample-use" argument is passed. Unfortunately, this ended up causing problems for the Linux kernel builds that are built with LLVM/Clang and with AutoFDO being used for the automatic feedback directed optimizations.

items.title: FAA Projects Busiest Thanksgiving Travel Week in 16 Years

Air traffic will dip only slightly on Wednesday (49,831 flights) and nearly halve on Thanksgiving Day (27,619 flights) itself, the FAA said, with a rebound following Friday to Tuesday, Dec.

items.title: TinyWifiDongle Arduino library turns ESP32-S3 and Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W boards into USB WiFi adapters
items.summary: TinyWifiDongle open-source Arduino library turns ESP32-S2/S3 and Raspberry Pi Pico W/2 W boards into USB WiFi adapters. The library uses USB CDC-NCM (Network Control Model) to provide network connectivity to Linux, macOS, and Windows 11 computers without installing additional drivers. The library implements a transparent Layer-2 bridge between the MCU’s WiFi and USB interfaces, allowing the connected computer to get an IP address directly from the router via DHCP, without NAT or a separate network.

items.title: Staffing Shortage Prompts Ground Stop at Chicago O’Hare
items.summary: The FAA temporarily halted flights bound for Chicago O’Hare International Airport on Monday after an air traffic control staffing shortage affected the facility responsible for managing arriving aircraft. The ground stop began at 10:40 a.m. Central and was lifted by approximately 12:15 p.m., according to the Chicago Sun-Times. “The FAA is briefly pausing flights into Chicago O’Hare International Airport due to staffing constraints at Chicago Terminal Radar Approach Control (TRACON),” the agency said in a statement to NBC Chicago.

items.title: American Airlines flight from San Diego to Chicago diverted to Phoenix Sky Harbor, passenger detained
items.summary: PHOENIX An American Airlines flight traveling from San Diego to Chicago was diverted to Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport overnight after air traffic controllers reported a "Level 3 threat" aboard the plane. The Federal Aviation Administration says AA flight 1494 landed safely in Phoenix around 1 a.m. after "a passenger disturbance on board." Details surrounding the incident remain limited at this time. Video from the scene shows that a man was detained following the diversion. We have reached out to more airline and local officials for additional details on this incident.

items.title: Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues
items.summary: Two of NASA's four missions operating at Mars have suspended science operations after encountering separate technical issues in recent weeks. The missions affected by the outages — hopefully temporary — are NASA's Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter. Both are operating beyond their original design lifetimes. Perseverance is in its sixth year exploring the surface of Mars, having collected rock and soil samples for eventual return to Earth. The rover is now studying the rim of a crater that once contained an ancient lake of liquid water.

items.title: Comet Encke's Shape and Heat Revealed in Thermal Glow
items.summary: Comets are time capsules of the origins of the solar system, containing materials that have existed for billions of years. While comets primarily orbit in the farthest reaches of the solar system, specifically the Kuiper Belt or Oort Cloud, some make their way closer to the Sun. When this happens, the increased heat cause cometary icy material to evaporate, producing a spectacular tail while also revealing the rocky material underneath, known as a comet’s nucleus. But how well can astronomers use telescopic observations to study the composition and temperatures of a cometary nucleus?

items.title: Teams Lock in Mission Architecture for NASA’s SR-1 Freedom
items.summary: 5 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) NASA completed a major review for Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom and locked in key elements of the spacecraft, which is targeted to launch in 2028 and demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion in deep space for the first time. Experts from across the agency, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), and industry met at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland for a major SR-1 mission design review in October. Several key decisions were made, propelling the mission from an early concept toward a defined spacecraft design.

items.title: Amateur Astronomer? Be a Kilonova Catcher!
items.summary: Explore This Section Science Citizen Science Amateur Astronomer? Be a… Overview Resources Opportunities Citizen Science Highlights About Science Activation Neutron stars are the ultra-dense, city-sized leftovers of dead stars. When they collide, they can release a brief flash of light called a kilonova. These immensely powerful events forge much of the universe’s gold, platinum and other heavy elements. Since a kilonova fades within days, astronomers have to find it fast, and no single observatory can watch the whole sky.

items.title: NASA’s Northrop Grumman CRS-25 Mission Overview
items.summary: NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission, or Northrop Grumman CRS-25, will deliver about 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station. The mission will be the third flight of the company’s Cygnus XL, the larger, more cargo-capable version of the company’s solar-powered spacecraft. The Cygnus XL will launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Following arrival to the station, astronauts aboard the space station will use the Canadarm2 to grapple the spacecraft before ground controllers robotically install it to the Unity module’s Earth-facing port for cargo unloading.

items.title: Amazon discovers Falcon 9 and Ariane 6 can deliver when nobody else can
items.summary: A European Ariane 6 launcher propelled 36 satellites into orbit for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation Tuesday, continuing the network's build-out after 40 satellites were lost earlier this month during a failure of United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket. The launch was an important rebound for Amazon, bringing the Amazon Leo fleet to 432 satellites as the company seeks to fill the void left by the grounding of ULA's Vulcan rocket, Amazon's primary launch provider. Now, an Amazon official tells Ars it is accelerating several Falcon 9 launches the company has purchased from SpaceX, which also owns the Starlink satellite network that Amazon seeks to dethrone.

items.title: Peppermint OS Launches Its First Void Linux-Based Release
items.summary: A little over a month after announcing PepVoid, Peppermint OS has released its first Void Linux-based edition, introducing a rolling-release alternative to the project’s Debian and Devuan offerings. The new edition amounts to a significant departure from Peppermint’s traditional technical foundation. Unlike Debian, Void Linux follows a rolling-release development model, uses its own XBPS package manager, and relies on runit rather than systemd for service management. Powered by the Linux kernel 6.18 LTS, the initial release retains the familiar Xfce desktop environment and comes as a Loaded edition, featuring a selection of preinstalled applications and utilities.

items.title: Cisco and OpenAI Unveil Shirudo, an eBPF-Based Linux Security Platform
items.summary: Cisco and OpenAI have introduced Shirudo, an open-source, eBPF-based security platform built to protect running Linux systems from the exploitation of vulnerabilities without requiring system restarts or interrupting applications. Developed in collaboration with Cisco’s Isovalent team, the project builds on the foundations of Tetragon, a Linux security observability and runtime enforcement tool, but has been redesigned to support AI-assisted vulnerability mitigation. The idea behind Shirudo is to narrow the exposure window between discovering a vulnerability and deploying a permanent security patch.

items.title: NASA may get $2 billion boost as White House seeks to accelerate Artemis
items.summary: As part of ongoing wrangling over the US budget for the current fiscal year, the White House on Monday night sent a list of budget exceptions to Congress that it seeks in the near term for the federal government ( PDF ). The list of so-called "funding anomalies" is dominated largely by appropriations for the Department of Defense, including the Golden Dome missile defense program championed by the Trump administration. However, among the highest non-defense exceptions is $2 billion for NASA's Artemis program for a "higher rate of operations."

items.title: Astronomers discover the most distant and ancient supermassive black hole-powered quasar in the universe
items.summary: The Euclid space telescope has spotted the most distant and ancient quasar ever seen, a bright cosmic event powered by a supermassive black hole with 360 million times the mass of the sun. The supermassive black hole is seen as it was just 630 million years after the Big Bang. 40 million years further back in time than the previous record holder for the most ancient quasar. The discovery further deepens the mystery of how supermassive black holes grew so massive so soon into the history of the universe.

items.title: Launch Preview: Russian, Chinese, and SpaceX rockets to launch space station missions
items.summary: Ten rockets are set to launch over the next week, with three visiting two different space stations in low-Earth orbit. Progress MS-36 and CRS NG-25 are expected to deliver supplies to the International Space Station, while Shenzhou 24 is scheduled to launch the next crew to the Chinese Tiangong Space Station, including its first international visitor. Outside of space station flights, Falcon 9 is set to launch a pair of USSF missions from Vandenberg, and China is set to launch a quadruple-header of payloads to orbit.

items.title: Hera mission spots asteroid eclipse. Plus, impact reveal today!
items.summary: Asteroid’s solar eclipse and livestream reveal It’s been 4 years since NASA’s DART spacecraft smashed into asteroid Dimorphos in a test of our planetary defense capabilities. And at 12:45 pm CST ( 18:45 UTC ) today, Wednesday, November 25, 2026, ESA will reveal the first close-up images of asteroid Dimorphos after the impact. items.title: Netflix Pulled Off the Impossible With This Unadaptable 3-Book Sci-Fi Series
items.summary: There’s a classical sentiment that “the book is always better than the adaptation,” but that isn’t always the case. Beyond the very obvious examples of all-time classics based on mediocre books, the transition to a new medium forces certain changes to tell the story in the most palatable way; books with a strong mythology and attention to detail can be more challenging to bring to life on screen, given that audiences don’t want to sit around having information painstakingly explained to them. 3 Body Problem is a remarkable adaptation because it retains the essence of the source material, yet grafts upon a multicultural story with a broader ensemble.

items.title: November's full moon dazzles skywatchers with a stunning Beaver Moon supermoon (photos)
items.summary: The November full moon rose to put on a spectacular natural light show on Nov. 24 and we've got the photos to prove it! Read on to see our favorite shots of the "Beaver Moon" captured from around the world. Each monthly full moon has its own set of informal names, often bestowed to reflect events occurring in the world at the time of their rising. The November moon is often known as the Beaver Moon, a name associated with the time of year when beavers prepare for winter and when trappers historically set beaver traps before waterways froze.

items.title: Upper Lake Mary rises from 16% to 82% full after Halloween rain
items.summary: ﻿ Upper Lake Mary in Flagstaff is now 82% full following Halloween rain. In early October, the reservoir had been drawn down to about 16%, its lowest level in two decades. Brian Huntzinger, water production manager with Flagstaff Water Services, told KTAR News 92.3 FM on Friday. He said the reservoir cannot be drawn down below 14.5%. “It was getting a little white-knuckle there,” Huntzinger said. Upper Lake Mary rose 50 percentage points the weekend of Oct. 31. “It’s pretty rare to have such an infill from rain alone in the fall for this time of year,” he said.

For now the Radeon kernel driver support in Mesa 27.0 is disabled by default but can be re-enabled, but eventually that Radeon kernel driver support by RadeonSI will be removed…

items.title: New FAA Rule For Planes Lining Up On Runways May Cause Delays
items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has just added some new restrictions to how air traffic controllers can clear aircraft to “line up and wait” on the runway, in anticipation of takeoff clearance. This is intended to add an extra safety buffer, but to quote an airline pilot on an ATC frequency, “that’s probably going to cause some delays, that’s for sure.” New restrictions on planes holding on runway for takeoff As of today (November 24, 2026), the FAA has introduced a new rule regarding how aircraft can be cleared onto runways at airports.

items.title: BepiColombo successfully enters orbit of Mercury, suffers orbit-altering software glitch
items.summary: At 18:24 UTC on Saturday, Nov. 21, the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency’s (JAXA) BepiColombo mission, comprising a stack of two spacecraft built by the two agencies, fired its thrusters to insert itself into orbit around Mercury. To say the moment was a long time coming would be an understatement — BepiColombo launched on Oct. 20, 2018, and has followed a complex trajectory to Mercury, conducting nine total gravity-assist flybys: one at Earth, two at Venus, and six at Mercury.

items.title: Glendale Glitters returns bigger than ever with 2.6 million lights and new displays in downtown Glendale
items.summary: Glendale Glitters is back and bigger than ever, returning to historic downtown Glendale on Friday with 2.6 million lights, new displays, and a newly renovated Murphy Park as its backdrop. Mayor Jerry Weiers and the Glendale City Council will kick off the festivities with a lighting ceremony beginning at 5:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 27, at Murphy Park, 5850 W. items.title: The King’s Unwilling Participants: Civilians and War in Medieval England
items.summary: Civilians supplied the money, food, ships and labour that kept medieval England’s armies fighting. items.title: What is a thought made of? Why human consciousness may be beyond AI’s reach
items.summary: A new theory suggests that the brain may chemically encode and retrieve memories rather than relying solely on electrical signals. items.title: Supercharging transformer residual connections
items.summary: We present DeepCrossAttention (DCA), an architecture that enhances transformer networks by using learnable weights and depth-wise cross-attention to dynamically combine outputs from previous layers, preventing the information dilution seen in traditional residual connections. Presented in our ICML 2025 paper, this architectural improvement allows models to achieve the same quality up to three times faster with a negligible increase in parameters. Think of a traditional deep learning model like a giant game of "Telephone": data passes through layer after layer, with each layer changing the information slightly.

items.title: Fed’s preferred inflation gauge accelerated to 3.8% in October, likely sealing rate hike
items.summary: Inflation moved further away from the Federal Reserve's target in October, reinforcing expectations that another interest rate hike is in cards for December and raising questions about how much more work the central bank will have to do in 2027. The personal consumption expenditures price index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, showed a seasonally adjusted 3.8% annual inflation rate, in line with the Dow Jones consensus estimate. Excluding food and energy, core PCE was 3.3%, which was 0.1 percentage point above the forecast, the Commerce Department reported Wednesday.

items.title: Kotlin Benchmark 2.0: How AI Coding Agents Handle Harder Tasks and Closed-Source Code
items.summary: In July, we released the Kotlin Benchmark – a collection of 105 real repository-level tasks for evaluating AI coding agents’ work with Kotlin. Since then, we’ve updated it to be more representative of what Kotlin teams do, with more reliable results and more data to help you choose an agent-model configuration. The new tasks require changes across multiple files, come from projects in different Kotlin domains, and include code from private repositories. To prevent reward hacking and improve the reliability of our results, we restricted network access when agents solve open-source tasks, so they can’t look up a fix that has already been published.

items.title: U.S. proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China and the EU
items.summary: The U.S. has proposed new tariffs on 14 partners including China, the European Union, Japan and India, as President Donald Trump doubles down on levies, despite a large chunk of his previous duties being struck down by the Supreme Court. The targeted economies create, sustain, or contribute to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors which burden or restrict American commerce, a senior U.S. official said. The 14 partners have been notified of these actions, with neither country's tariffs exceeding rates announced as part of framework deals on reciprocal trade, the official added.

items.title: The Fed is likely to raise rates in December. What it means for your holiday spending
items.summary: New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said Monday that policymakers have more work to do to bring inflation under control — signaling that the central bank may raise interest rates and borrowing costs for consumers during the peak holiday spending season. Williams' comments were likely the last major policy statement from a Fed official before the Federal Open Market Committee's Dec. 8-9 meeting. As of Tuesday, investors were pricing in a 97% chance of an interest rate hike, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool, with a quarter-percentage-point increase expected.

items.title: China investigates Politburo member and Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
items.summary: BANGKOK — Chinese Communist Party authorities are investigating Shanghai party secretary Chen Jining for suspected violations of party discipline, China's anti-corruption watchdog said Tuesday. The Politburo member is the latest senior official targeted in President Xi Jinping's long-running anti-corruption campaign, which has shown no signs of letting up in scope or depth. A statement released by the Shanghai city government said the Standing Committee of the Shanghai Committee of the CCP "expressed firm support" for the decision to investigate Chen.

items.title: IBM quantum computer solves problem classical computers can’t in just 15 minutes
items.summary: IBM and University of Chicago researchers have demonstrated that a quantum computer can complete an extraordinarily complex calculation in just 15 minutes, beyond the practical reach of leading classical computing methods. A novel error-detection technique also allows scientists to establish confidence in the accuracy of the results, overcoming a major hurdle in quantum computing.

items.title: the search for a home without a fixed address, from prefabricated houses to floating dwellings
items.summary: THE IDEA OF A HOME WITHOUT A FIXED ADDRESS For decades, architects have imagined homes that can be packed up, transported, and assembled somewhere new, designing alternatives to the idea that housing must be tied to a permanent address. From prefabricated dwellings designed for mass production to experimental houses conceived for remote landscapes, these projects explore how architecture might exist beyond the limits of a fixed site. One early expression of this ambition came from American architect and inventor Buckminster Fuller.

items.title: nick cave and india pavilion win the visitors’ lions at the venice art biennale 2026
items.summary: Visitors choose their favorites at the 2026 venice art biennale The public has selected its favorites at the 61st Venice Art Biennale, with American artist Nick Cave receiving the Visitors’ Lion for Best Participant and India winning Best National Participation for its pavilion, Geographies of Distance: Remembering Home. items.title: human point frames architecture as an unfolding timeline
items.summary: HUMAN POINT CHOREOGRAPHS SPACE AROUND HUMAN PRESENCE With three decades of practice behind it, Human Point approaches the built environment as a living sequence shaped by human presence. Spanning architecture, urban planning, real estate development, investment strategy, engineering, and turn-key construction, the multidisciplinary practice integrates architectural vision, technical expertise, and economic thinking into a unified approach, from initial concept to completed development.

items.title: Debian wakes up wearing Windows XP's actual skin
items.summary: Win4Wine is one of the more remarkable and creative hacks we've read about in recent years. It runs Windows XP's genuine Explorer shell through patched Wine on Debian 13, with a custom window manager integrating Linux applications into the desktop. As its GitHub repository explains: "The taskbar, Start menu, desktop and folder windows are XP's real ones, and Linux applications get XP's frames and taskbar buttons." This impressive, possibly demented project has English installation instructions and a README, although its design documents are in Japanese.

items.title: Two tech companies tried to reinvent the e-bike. Why DJI’s Amflow soared while Rivian’s ALSO floundered
items.summary: Two of the most interesting new electric bicycle companies in the world made headlines on the same day last week, and for two very different reasons. Amflow, the electric bicycle brand that emerged from the same engineering ecosystem responsible for DJI’s revolutionary Avinox drive system, just launched its first commuter e-bike to widespread acclaim. Meanwhile, ALSO, the high-tech electric bicycle startup spun out of Rivian, announced that it was halting deliveries of its futuristic TM-B electric bicycle amid mounting software problems. more…

items.title: The Porsche Boxster EV is finally almost here, and it will be the most powerful 718 yet
items.summary: The first fully electric Porsche Boxster is finally in the home stretch of development. Ahead of its official debut in early 2027, Porsche offered an early look at the two-door electric sports car. Despite rumors that the all-electric 718 Boxster was canceled, Porsche confirmed on Tuesday that the Boxster EV will debut in the first quarter of 2027. “Starting next year, the all-electric 718 Boxster will offer our customers a compelling entry point into the world of two-door sports cars,” Porsche CEO Dr Michael Leiters said.

items.title: Liesman: Nvidia whiplash tests Kevin Warsh’s push to read market signals
items.summary: The extreme market gyrations and the drama surrounding Nvidia this past week have highlighted the dilemma facing Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh. On Friday, as stocks sold off, market-based probabilities that the Fed would raise interest rates declined. On Monday, with Jensen Huang back in office, a powerful rally restored market confidence that two more rate hikes are coming. On one level, ignoring daily market vicissitudes and focusing on the long term is at the heart of one of the key changes Warsh wants to push through at the Fed.

items.title: Sticker Shock Looms as a Major Challenge in Push for Single-Payer Healthcare
items.summary: As an Oregon panel finalized its proposal for statewide universal healthcare this month, opposition had already coalesced around a familiar theme: The costs and the new taxes needed to support it will be staggeringly large. The panel’s estimates place the cost of the plan at $69.7 billion a year starting in 2032. The same arguments are being made on the national level about “Medicare for All,” which gained renewed life after Democrats’ victorious blue wave in the midterms. One recent White House cost estimate pegged the annual price tag at $4.7 trillion.

items.title: Where to Eat Along Slovenia’s Alpe Adria Trail, From Milka to Hiša Franko
items.summary: Explore the full trail S lovenia’s stages of the Alpe Adria Trail pass some of the country’s best cooking, from Michelin-starred dining rooms to village inns serving river trout and mountain cheese. Slovenia’s two most decorated restaurants sit about 37 miles (60 km), or a three days’ walk, apart on the trail: Milka in Kranjska Gora (two Michelin stars) and Hiša Franko in Kobarid (three). Book Milka the night before Stage 23. Hiša Franko sits in Kobarid, in the valley below Drežnica, so plan it as a rest-day dinner or arrange a transfer through the Booking Center.

items.title: 'I only use the washing machine on a Sunday' - how we're keeping our energy bills down
items.summary: Domestic energy prices will soar by 26% in January under the regulator Ofgem's new price cap, pushing up bills for millions of households across England, Scotland and Wales. With household budgets already under pressure, finding ways to reduce gas and electricity costs has become increasingly important. But how much difference can simple changes really make? The BBC spoke to three people about what they're doing to keep their energy costs down. Like many people, Kelly Anne Harvey, a building surveyor from Cleveleys near Blackpool, is worried about her energy bill going up next year.

items.title: Mitsubishi Electric Research Lab CEO on How He Reached the C-Suite
items.summary: The trajectory from researcher to top executive at a leading R&D organization doesn’t happen overnight. It took Anthony Vetro nearly 30 years to climb the corporate ladder at Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories, in Cambridge, Mass. He joined MERL in 1996, right out of college, and he has worked there ever since. Vetro probably is best known for his research in multimedia signal processing, focusing on video compression. items.title: A desert city's quest to curb water waste and lower bills as shortage looms
items.summary: When Frank Bencomo was growing up, his family struggled to pay the water bill. On a warm October morning during a home visit, he saw echoes of his own childhood. At a modest house near the Tucson high school he attended, a disabled Vietnam War veteran raising two grandchildren frowned at a water bill topping $100. Bencomo inspected the homes water meter, pipes and two toilets, adjusted a loose valve that kept water running slowly from the tank, and showed the mans 11-year-old grandson how to address a leaking toilet, which often makes a hissing sound.

items.summary: Influenza vaccination after a heart attack can reduce the risk of death during the following year. This has been shown in previous research from Sweden and international collaborations.

items.title: Court-appointed medical guardian study reveals role in care of highly vulnerable older adults
items.summary: When University of Michigan Health geriatrician Kahli Zietlow, M.D., gets summoned to the hospital room of a seriously ill older adult, she knows the assessments she performs might help determine if the patient can make their own medical decisions or if someone else will have to. But if the patient's health or mental capacity has declined too far before they could legally authorize someone to make medical decisions for them, then Zietlow knows that the hospital may ask a probate court to assign a guardian to make those decisions, either temporarily or permanently.

items.title: Zimbabwe issues arrest warrant for Robert Mugabe's son over missed court date
items.summary: A Zimbabwean court has issued an arrest warrant for Bellarmine Chatunga Mugabe, the youngest son of the country's late former president Robert Mugabe, after he failed to appear in court. Mugabe was arrested earlier this month alongside four others over assault allegations on a police officer during an investigation into the suspected smuggling of luxury vehicles. The group subsequently faced charges of robbery and malicious damage to property. They have yet to enter pleas. They were granted bail on 6 November and were due back in court on Tuesday.

items.title: Study Suggests People Traveled Long Distances to Roman Britain’s First Capital
items.summary: DURHAM, ENGLAND—According to a statement released by Durham University, analysis of strontium and lead isotopes in cremated remains recovered from 2,000-year-old burials in Colchester, the first capital of Roman Britannia, indicates that several of the 22 individuals grew up thousands of miles away. Joanna Moore, Janet Montgomery, and Geoff Nowell of Durham University and their colleagues developed a way to analyze isotopes in remains that had been subjected to the intense heat generated by funeral pyres.

items.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
items.summary: Our GPT‑6 family of models can design new protein shapes and the sequence of their chemical building blocks using only reasoning and code, without calling specialized biology models to generate those designs. An internal research model matched or outperformed specialized models on many protein design tasks. Researchers could also guide designs by prompting the model on where a protein should attach and what shape it should take. In lab tests with Onava, proteins based on GPT‑6.2’s designs showed evidence of binding, or attachment, across five targets.

items.title: Army Looks to Resume Helicopter Training Near Reagan National
items.summary: The U.S. Army is looking to resume helicopter training flights near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA), less than two years after a midair collision between an Army helicopter and a regional jet killed 67 people. items.title: Gallowglass: The Scottish Mercenaries Who Shaped Irish History
items.summary: Armed with formidable battle axes, Scotland’s gallowglass mercenaries became a powerful force in medieval Ireland’s rivalries. Brendan Farrell traces how these warriors won land, served competing clans and helped shape Irish history. How elite Scottish warriors determined the course of Irish history; Immortalised by Dürer and Shakespeare but largely forgotten, these Scottish ‘Samurai’ deserve their place in history. Late medieval Ireland could be an extremely dangerous place! The English had yet to bring it to heel, and power was mercurial.

The number of cases in the capital of Rio de Janeiro is more than 22 times higher than the number reported during the same period in 2025.

items.title: Greetings from Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest point in all its splendor
items.summary: As dawn broke one recent morning over camp, we got one of our first full views of the peak of Mount Kilimanjaro, normally hidden behind clouds. Climbing tall mountains like Kilimanjaro is a study in contrasts. The beating sun bakes you during the day, walking so close to the equator, but the nights quickly dip below freezing. Snow remains constantly in sight from humid rainforest and alpine landscapes, freshly charred from a wildfire three weeks before. And always beckoning is the peak, within sight, but seemingly never nearer; the high altitude means hikers need to walk slowly or else risk exhaustion and altitude sickness.

items.title: Chartres Cathedral: Relics, Vikings and Sacred Music
items.summary: According to medieval tradition, the Virgin Mary’s tunic helped the people of Chartres repel a Viking attack. Sonja Maurer-Dass explores how devotion to this sacred relic shaped the cathedral’s identity and inspired influential Marian chants. Within its walls, the Pinacoteca di Brera in Milan houses a peculiar battle scene painted by seventeenth-century Italian artist Padovanino (born Alessandro Varotari). The painting, titled The Victory of the Carnutes Over the Normans (1618), depicts an event from the historical siege of Chartres in 911.

items.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
items.summary: Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server. The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework. The hackers, who provided prompts in simplified Chinese and configured the model to the Chinese Standard Time zone, gave the agents a list of IP addresses and the goal: “obtain shell access.” In short order, the agents discovered a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application running on one of the target servers.

items.summary: The Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association (AOPA) Air Safety Institute has released its 36th Richard G. McSpadden Report last week, which found that both the overall and fatal general aviation accident rates declined in 2024, continuing a broader downward trend in GA accidents over the past decade. According to the report, general aviation recorded 1,064 accidents in 2024, 164 of which were fatal. The overall accident rate fell to 3.69 per 100,000 flight hours, down from 3.86 in 2023, while the fatal accident rate declined from 0.65 to 0.57.

items.title: Bickering Buildings: A Dialogue Between the Churches of Athens in 1854
items.summary: The churches of Athens had much to say in 1854, when an anonymous author staged a squabble between them in newsprint. Nikos Magouliotis eavesdrops on this chatter, finding personified anxieties about Greek architectural identity, foreign influence, and the newly formed nation’s relation to its past.

items.title: Macdonald Book Shop in Estes Park, Colorado
items.summary: At Macdonald Book Shop, a cozy and beloved store in the Colorado mountain town of Estes Park, selling books began as a side hustle. J. Edward Macdonald bought a small log cabin in Estes Park in 1908 and opened a hardware and general store next door — with one corner full of books for sale. When he retired, his wife Jessica turned the parlor of their home into a proper bookstore, also selling magazines, stationery, and school supplies. That was 1928. Books have been the focus ever since. Over the decades, the shop expanded to claim more of the original house.

items.title: Veteran Nigerian Nollywood actor Pete Edochie dies aged 79
items.summary: Veteran Nigerian actor Pete Edochie, one of Africa's most celebrated film stars, has died at the age of 79, his family has announced. Known for his deep voice, commanding screen presence and memorable use of African proverbs, Edochie became a household name across Africa, often portraying powerful traditional rulers, wealthy businessmen and family patriarchs. In a statement, his family said Edochie died in the early hours of Wednesday in the south-eastern Nigerian city of Enugu following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer.

items.title: More Than a Ski Trip: The Mountain Towns That Stayed With Us.
items.summary: More Than a Ski Trip: The Mountain Towns That Stayed With Us. M ountain towns in winter get filed under one thing: skiing. But often, the reason that a certain town sticks with you is about more than just the snow. It might be the personal connection you felt with a server who knew your breakfast order by the third morning, the hot spring that fixed your bad mood, or the strangers on the chairlifts who turned into unexpected hosts. The skiing may be why you book the trip, but it’s the towns that’ll keep you coming back year after year.

items.title: 'Haru to Gen ~70-sai, Hajimete Kosodate~' Anime's Teaser Reveals More Cast, Ending Song
items.summary: Jin Urayama, HItomi Shogawa, Nao Shiraki, Akiko Seri join cast with music by Kuricorder Quartet…

items.title: How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops
items.summary: The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this "smoke taint" adversely affected not only local wine production, but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant. That's why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews.

items.title: Army to detonate tons of lead azide after delays. And, Abrego Garcia leaves U.S.
items.summary: The Army will detonate a huge explosion in Middletown, Iowa, this morning to safely dispose of thousands of pounds of lead azide that could spontaneously explode. The explosive has been used since WWI and was moved to the Iowa bunker 17 years ago. The detonation is happening after officials found that the lead azide had crystallized and become unstable. Authorities have evacuated a 5-mile radius, and those within 20 miles are advised to stay indoors to avoid exposure to toxins. Kilmar Abrego Garcia has voluntarily left the U.S. after a nearly two-year legal battle.

items.title: NATO to deploy AWACS aircraft as Russian airspace violations in Poland continue
items.summary: NATO will forward-deploy one of its Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) aircraft following the incursion of three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles into Polish airspace on November 20, 2026, the alliance announced after a meeting of the North Atlantic Council in Brussels. The announcement came shortly before Poland reported another violation of its airspace by a Russian drone on November 23, 2026, prompting its military to authorize the use of weapons before ultimately deciding against shooting down the aircraft.

items.title: Black Diamond Coefficient Hoody Review
items.summary: Bottom Line The Black Diamond Coefficient Hoody ( men’s / women’s ) is a high-output specialist. On an overcast, 45-degree-Fahrenheit hike on the Sierra Front Trail in Reno, we climbed steadily in the Coefficient over a tank top without needing to unzip it to cool off. The gridded fleece released heat better than both the Patagonia Micro D Pullover or Outdoor Research Vigor Plus Hoodie we tested alongside it. If you run warm or spend most of the day moving, that breathable construction is the reason to buy it.

items.title: Patagonia Micro D Pullover Review
items.summary: Bottom Line The Patagonia Micro D Pullover ( men’s / women’s ) is a comfortable, uncomplicated fleece for anyone who wants a little extra warmth without carrying a heavy layer. Of the three fleeces we tested side by side, it offered the softest traditional fleece feel and landed between the Black Diamond Coefficient and Outdoor Research Vigor Plus for warmth. After a five-mile trail run in the Reno foothills at around 50 degrees Fahrenheit, we pulled it on over sweaty clothing and quickly shook off the chill.

items.title: Why Did Arapaho Warrior Woman Pretty Nose Fight at Little Bighorn?
items.summary: The Battle of the Little Bighorn holds a unique place in American history, and remains etched into the collective psyche of Americans even today. The actions carried out on that day by Crazy Horse, George Custer, and Chief Gall will never be forgotten. However, one participant remains overlooked. She is Pretty Nose, a young warrior who became a war chief. From Manitoba Farmers to Master Horsemen on the Great Plains Pretty Nose was born in 1851 to the Arapaho people, who originally inhabited the area that is now the province of Manitoba, Canada.

items.title: I can now pause my Pi-hole with an ESP32 (and 3 more cheap network projects I'm working on next)
items.summary: Many homelab projects can get quite expensive—it's why I don't do nearly as many of them as I'd like to. But an ESP32 is actually the perfect cheap upgrade for your homelab's network because of how capable (and low-cost) it is. ESP32 development boards have built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, allowing them to connect to your network and receive or send various bits of information. That means that you can use an ESP32 to serve data to your homelab, like as a network time server, or to receive information from your homelab, such as to display stats on a small OLED screen.

items.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
items.summary: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this: In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count.

items.title: Arizona certifies its 2026 midterm election results
items.summary: Arizona officially certified the results of the 2026 midterm election Monday morning. The state’s counties certified their results last week, allowing for the recount process to begin for a small number of close races. Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap did not attend his county’s certification and opted to hold his own press conference certifying the results last week. Heap, who consistently voted in the state legislature for election denier bills, has been feuding with the Maricopa County Board of Supervisors over control of the office.

items.title: US Army Moves To Restart Washington DC Helicopter Training Flights 2 Years After Deadly Crash
items.summary: The US Army is moving to resume helicopter training flights in airspace near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA) as soon as the week of December 6, according to a recent report by Politico. That timeline comes less than two years after the January 29, 2025 midair collision between an Army Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk and a PSA Airlines regional jet operating as American Airlines Flight 5342 over the Potomac River, a disaster that killed all 67 people aboard both aircraft.

items.title: Quantum blueprint maps a practical path to testing unusual entanglement
items.summary: Adrian Del Maestro knows how to engineer a quantum fingerprint. Rick Mukherjee has a gift for tuning atoms. Their combined expertise has taken a theory sketched out on paper and created a pathway for real experiments. The results, published in the journal Physical Review Letters, move a law-defying "mathematical oddity" ever so slightly up the technology readiness scale…

items.title: Free Fall
items.summary: In contemplating the theory of general relativity, Albert Einstein imagined a falling lift in which people are performing experiments: One of the observers takes a handkerchief and a watch from his pocket and drops them. What happens to these two bodies? … or the outside observer they are both falling with the same acceleration. But so is the lift, with its walls, ceiling, and floor. Therefore: the distance between the two bodies and the floor will not change. This notion of the equivalence between gravity and acceleration, which he called “the happiest thought of my life,” came to Einstein in 1907.

items.title: Russia issued flight ban ahead of Romanian F-16 strike on Black Sea drone
items.summary: Romanian Air Force F-16s carried out a mission against an explosive-laden maritime drone near the Neptun Deep offshore gas project on August 20, 2026, despite Russia announcing a flight ban over the area, former Romanian Defense Minister Radu Miruță has revealed. Miruță made the disclosure on SpotMedia’s Controverse podcast, in an interview published on November 24, 2026. He said the Russian notification arrived shortly after he ordered fighter jets to engage the drone, announcing that Moscow was imposing flight restrictions over the area.

items.title: Man shot at Phoenix light rail station; suspect remains at large
items.summary: PHOENIX (AZFamily) — A man is expected to survive after he was pistol-whipped and shot in the neck at a Phoenix light rail station Sunday morning, police said. The shooter remains at large. Police said an argument between two people on the platform at the Metro Parkway station turned violent just before 9 a.m. Surveillance video sent to Arizona’s Family shows two people appearing to fight. The suspect appears to strike the victim in the head with a gun, point the weapon, and fire before running away.

items.title: A new reason for magic numbers: Scientists discover the secret behind an unusually stable molecular cluster
items.summary: Why are some groups of molecules remarkably stable while others readily break apart? Researchers at Bar-Ilan University have discovered a surprising explanation for why clusters containing exactly six molecules of glycine, the simplest amino acid, are exceptionally stable—making six a "magic number." Moreover, they have uncovered the reason for this increased stability. The secret lies in a transformation that takes place when the molecules come together: they change their structure and become zwitterions, allowing them to form stronger bonds with one another.

items.title: Homo erectus lived in the rainforest alongside Denisovans
items.summary: Homo erectus was walking around mainland Asia at least 60,000 years more recently than archaeologists thought. A handful of teeth from two caves in southern China's Guangxi Province just filled in a significant gap in the fossil record of a region that's vital to the story of how our genus, Homo, took over the world. The chemical makeup of the teeth's enamel suggests that, over the course of their lives, these Homo erectus moved across surprisingly large distances and made their living in dense tropical rainforests—an environment we'd previously assumed that only our species had ever gained a real foothold in.

items.title: This man sometimes sees his cat’s eyes on people’s faces
items.summary: After returning home from a 2024 brain surgery, a man started noticing something strange: Eyes that he had previously seen started showing up on the face he was currently looking at. To his bewilderment, the swapping of features even extended to his pet cat Luna. “Right when I got home from the hospitals, I was seeing my cat in my mother and my sister,” says the 29-year-old teacher, who has asked to go by Karl to protect his privacy. “That was one of the first things that I noticed,” he says. “And the cat even took on resemblances of people.”

items.title: In a time of rising costs, one Thanksgiving commodity is cheaper: cannabis
items.summary: This Thanksgiving season, Americans are paying more for almost everything: travel costs have soared, and the price of food has risen. Bringing wine to the family dinner? That costs more, too. But there's one thing consumers buy at high rates that will actually get cheaper this time of year: marijuana. Known in the industry as "Green Week" or "Green Wednesday," the days ahead of Thanksgiving have come to rival famed stoner holiday 4/20 as the day cannabis dispensaries see the most sales — and highest foot traffic — of the year.

items.title: Space entrepreneurs should look to 16th-century spice trade for inspiration
items.summary: Despite all the hype about a new space economy, humanity has yet to reap much benefit from off-world mining, manufacturing or space tourism.

items.title: What Did Children in a Greek Colony Eat 2,500 Years Ago?
items.summary: ATHENS, GEORGIA—Analysis of 2,500-year-old remains unearthed in the Greek colony of Himera on the island of Sicily suggests that babies began eating solid food at about three months of age, but were not fully weaned until they were almost four years old, Phys.org reports. This is similar to the weaning practices found at Apollonia Pontica, a Greek colony on the Black Sea coast. More than 13,000 burials have been excavated at Himera, but infant and child mortality appeared to be low among the population, which was made up of Sicilians, Phoenicians, and Greeks.

items.title: Evolution keeps returning to simple leaves
items.summary: A study led by researchers from the University of Oxford has explained a long-standing riddle: why do most plants have leaves with a very simple shape? In a new study published Nov. 24, they explain why complex leaves have evolved again and again—only for evolution to repeatedly revert to simpler forms.

items.title: Turkish Air Force Cougar helicopter crashes, killing five personnel
items.summary: Five Turkish Air Force personnel were killed when an AS532 Cougar helicopter crashed during a training flight in the western province of Eskisehir on November 24, 2026, Turkey’s Ministry of National Defense said. In a statement published the same day, the ministry said the helicopter had crashed “for a reason not yet determined.” An earlier statement said the aircraft had taken off from Eskisehir, that rescuers had reached the wreckage and that search and rescue operations were underway. The ministry identified those killed as two pilots, and three noncommissioned officers, including an aircraft maintenance technician.

items.title: The 7 Most Powerful City-States That Fought in the Trojan War
items.summary: The Trojan War in The Iliad, as told by Homer, is one of the foundational literary works of Western civilization. While there is no direct evidence to support some specifics of the war, like the Trojan Horse, there is archaeological evidence for the existence of the city of Troy and its destruction in modern-day Turkey. Furthermore, many of the city-states that are said to have fought in the war are historically known to us, such as Mycenae, Argos, Pylos, Xanthos, Knossos, Thebes, and Miletus. 1.

items.title: Autonomous Black Hawk Demonstrates Obstacle Avoidance
items.summary: Near Earth Autonomy announced Monday that its optionally piloted RUC-60 Black Hawk helicopter completed a series of autonomous flight exercises Nov. 19 at Tullahoma Regional Airport in Tennessee, demonstrating its ability to detect and avoid obstacles and adapt to changes in mission objectives while airborne. During the exercise, ground-based operators directed the helicopter through missions beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS), issuing holding commands from distances exceeding 45 nautical miles.

items.title: The Incredible, Elegant DNA Repair System Makes Gene Editing Work
items.summary: Humans have debated the meaning of life for many millennia, but from evolution’s perspective, it is simple: Preserve the genome. Of course, mutation is allowed, as is the genetic mixing and matching of sexual reproduction, to create variety and evolutionary diversity. But we all exist because a viable lineage of DNA has persisted for 4 billion years. The genome’s policy is typically… Source…

items.title: Math’s holy grail, the Riemann hypothesis, appears solved with AI’s help
items.summary: A long-sought pinnacle of mathematics has apparently been reached. In a feat that will go down in mathematics history, a human working with AI appears to have solved the most famous puzzle in math, proving the Riemann hypothesis. The problem has foiled repeated and valiant attempts at solution for more than a century. Now, mathematicians are working to understand the proof, posted by Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, on November 20. The Riemann hypothesis, if true, reveals the secrets of prime numbers.

items.title: 57 Food Gifts We’re Giving (and Secretly Hoping to Get) in 2026
items.summary: It’s never too early to get a head start on holiday gifting. After all, getting your shopping done now means you can focus on the important things once the holidays actually roll around—you know, like spending time with family, cooking a festive feast, and enjoying plenty of mulled cider and wine. If you’re in need of gifts for the food people in your life, look no further. These are the 57 gifts we’re planning to give (or hoping to receive) this year. A handmade mug is a little luxury they’ll use every day (and think of you when they do!).

items.title: K2 Aviation strengthens portfolio with purchase of six Boeing aircraft from SMBC
items.summary: Dublin-based K2 Aviation is strengthening its aircraft portfolio with the acquisition of six Boeing 737-800 Next Generation aircraft from SMBC Aviation Capital. On November 24, 2026, K2 Aviation confirmed that the two lessors had signed a definitive agreement for the aircraft which are currently on lease to six airline customers. K2 Aviation said that the “portfolio is diversified across Europe, Latin America, Asia, the Middle East and Africa”. In September 2026, K2 Aviation also signed an agreement with Carlyle Aviation Partners to purchase six Airbus and Boeing aircraft on lease to five airline customers.

items.title: Physicists trap antimatter in a breakthrough that could explain why the universe exists
items.summary: Positrons are the antimatter counterpart of an electron. Physicists trapped a positron and cooled it to temperatures near absolute zero. Positron is suspended in a wall-free trap, safely separated from ordinary matter. Team will conduct most precise comparison yet between matter and antimatter. Any difference between the electron and positron could expose cracks in the Standard Model of particle physics.

items.title: Yoga Horror Film ‘Namaslay’ Strikes a Pose on Digital This December
items.summary: Namaste. If you enjoy both horror and yoga, then you’ll want to keep an eye out for Namaslay, striking a pose on Digital on December 15th via Junghal Studios. Here’s the official synopsis: After arriving in Los Angeles, Gayatri accepts an invitation from her friend Judy to try an upscale yoga studio she’s been dying to attend. When the owner, Reyna, offers Gayatri a chance to join her instructor training program, Gayatri decides to look past the obvious eccentricities and accept the job.

items.title: Gothic survival horror metroidvania 'Shadow Sacrament: The Roots of Evil' shown off at the Horror Game Awards
items.summary: Eldritch House, the team behind Elderand, showed off a new trailer for Shadow Sacrament: The Roots of Evil at The Horror Game Awards 2026. It's a 2D gothic survival horror game with a bit of Metroidvania in it, and the new footage gives us a closer look at some of the nastier things you'll run into. You play a detective investigating a grisly crime at a remote monastery in the 19th century. You'll explore the monastery and its grounds, solving puzzles and picking your way through interconnected areas as you find out what happened there.

items.title: Su Blackwell Enchants with Folkloric Stories That Spring from Vintage Books
items.summary: From vintage tomes and encyclopedic volumes, British artist Su Blackwell carves, slices, and reconfigures text-laden pages into enchanting sculptures. Her latest body of work, opening this week in a solo show titled Pathway of Crumbs, draws on fairytales and folklore, a fitting topic for such dreamlike scenes. Nodding to the enduring children’s story of Hansel and Gretel, the exhibition roots in nature and the stories we draw from the world around us. “In Flight,” for example, stretches nearly 3.5 feet as a swarm of butterflies emerges from the flared pages of a book.

items.title: Major US East Coast storm threatens Thanksgiving flights from Atlanta to Boston
items.summary: A powerful coastal storm is expected to disrupt Thanksgiving flights along the US East Coast, bringing rain to Atlanta on Wednesday before heavy rain and strong winds reach Washington, Philadelphia, New York and Boston on Thanksgiving Day. The National Weather Service says gusts could reach 70 mph along the Eastern Seaboard. The storm is expected to strengthen off the Southeast coast on November 25 and move north through Thanksgiving. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said thunderstorms could affect Florida and the Gulf Coast on Wednesday, with rain possible at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) before wet weather spreads into the Mid-Atlantic later in the day.

Isaac, a student at Durham University, said he had no choice but to keep the heating in his student house on 'constantly' due to poor insulation, and he was not looking forward to the price increase. In the Autumn budget, the government announced a one-off payment of Â£100 for households in council bands A to D, 'half a weekly shop' according to Isaac.

items.title: US plans to hike tariffs on China, EU, Brazil and others over subsidized production
items.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump’s administration is planning to hike tariffs on Chinese goods by an additional 20% and raise import taxes on products from the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and nine other major trading partners. The new tariffs are meant to discourage excessive manufacturing output in those economies, boosted by subsidies and other trade barriers that the Republican administration says put American manufacturers at a disadvantage. The taxes are also intended to help replace the tariff revenues lost after the Supreme Court ruled in February that Trump could not declare an economic emergency to bypass Congress and impose across-the-board tariffs.

items.title: Trump’s Transportation Department Announces Record-Breaking Thanksgiving Air Travel for 2026
items.summary: WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Transportation Department’s Federal Aviation Administration today released the 2026 flight forecast ahead of Thanksgiving travel, projecting the busiest holiday skies in 16 years. The Trump Administration is working around the clock to ensure the flying public gets where they need to go this week — including standing up a Tiger Team — to maintain the safest and most efficient aviation system in the world. More than 417,000 flights are forecast over the nine-day holiday period.

items.title: Kimchi Bolognese
items.summary: I’ve always loved Italian American food. Maybe because Italian and Korean cooking have traits in common: Both are homey and resourceful, and grandmothers are revered for their signature dishes made without formal recipes. This recipe was one of the first Korean Italian fusion recipes I developed, and it makes use of my two favorite secret weapons: kimchi and fish sauce. The result is the Bolognese you know and love, but with a deep, tangy twist. Fish sauce in Italian cooking is not a new idea, actually—Romans have been using salted anchovies and garum, an ancient kind of fish sauce, for centuries.

items.title: COP31 ends in failure as countries split over fossil fuels, climate finance
items.summary: ANTALYA, Turkey—By the time the United Nations COP31 climate talks ended Sunday afternoon, the conference center resembled a going-out-of-business sale at a pawnshop for broken dreams. As cleaning crews cleared away the debris left by more than 100,000 participants, Murat Kurum, president of the Conference of the Parties and Turkey’s minister of environment, urbanization, and climate change, tried to tie together disparate parts of a draft climate deal with a shiny ribbon of multilateralism. Many countries were not buying it. Read full article Comments…

items.title: Trinity Rodman out of USWNT’s World Cup qualifier due to shoulder injury
items.summary: Trinity Rodman has not been included in the United States women’s national team squad for a qualifying tournament for the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 because of a minor shoulder injury. Rodman, 24, was injured on Saturday early in the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current in the NWSL Championship Game — the Spirit’s third consecutive setback in the title match. She was challenging for a ball when Current defender Laney Rouse collided with her midair and sent Rodman hard to the ground.

items.title: From solving to ‘digesting’: How mathematicians can adapt to the dramatic changes AI has brought to their field
items.summary: Mathematics is having an existential crisis. On Nov. 20, 2026, a mathematician at the AI company Anthropic claimed that while working with the model Claude, he had solved the generalized Riemann hypothesis, the most famous problem in mathematics. This problem has stood unsolved for 167 years, and solving it could easily warrant a Fields Medal – considered equivalent to a Nobel Prize, but for mathematics. In its current state, however, the solution is roughly 250,000 pages long, so it will take a while before human mathematicians can be satisfied that it is correct.

items.title: On a Ranch in Wyoming, a Stressed-Out Editor Gets in Sync With a Lazy Horse
items.summary: I used to avoid horses the same way I’d avoid palm readers. While my friends chased $5 readings in Downtown Manhattan, I preferred to keep the velvet curtain closed. I was convinced that once a fortune teller held my hands in hers, she would trace a life line abruptly cut short or reveal a heart line splintered beyond repair. So I’d sit on the stoop, hands safely secured in the pockets of my jacket. Horses and psychics, I believed, shared the same dark, all-knowing eyes. The first time I rode a horse was 10 years ago in Costa Rica, my body clenched for the entirety of the 20-minute sunset beach stroll.

items.title: ‘The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power’ Is Officially Renewed for Season 4
items.summary: With the final two episodes of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power season three arriving today, Prime Video has made it official: season four is coming. This isn’t a huge shock; showrunners J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay have long stated they have a five-season plan for the J.R.R. Tolkien adaptation, and the streamer has been supportive of the fantasy series it spent big bucks to acquire and produce. So today’s announcement is more of a formality than breaking news. According to a Prime Video press release, season four is actually already in pre-production, which tracks with the rumors earlier this year that development was well underway.

items.title: Africa Cup title given back to Senegal after sports court rules against Morocco
items.summary: More than 10 months on from a chaotic, controversial final, Senegal is Africa's soccer champion once again. Senegal won back the Africa Cup of Nations title in a legal fight on Tuesday after the Court of Arbitration for Sport overturned an earlier ruling which handed the trophy to Morocco. Senegal won the Africa Cup on the field in Morocco in January and then lost it in a legal case in March because its players walked off the field in protest in second-half stoppage time. CAS has now rejected that earlier ruling, based on referee Jean-Jacques Ndala's decision to let the game resume after the protest.

items.title: The Map of Ancient Philosophy: Animation Shows How Socrates, Aristotle, Confucius, the Buddha & Other Great Thinkers Fit Together
items.summary: Here on Open Culture, we’ve often featured the charming and informative posters of Domain of Science. Each one maps out a different field of knowledge: there’s biology, physics, chemistry, quantum physics, quantum computing, fungi, and many others besides. But with his latest map, Domain of Science creator Dominic Walliman has turned away from the scientific realm — or rather, he’s ventured into the larger intellectual territory out of which it emerged.

items.title: The Six Biggest Takeaways From COP31, Which Ended Without an Agreement After Talks Broke Down
items.summary: Representatives of nearly 200 countries gathered in Antalya, Turkey, this month for the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (known as COP31) to negotiate how the world should respond to an increasingly urgent climate crisis. Instead, the proceedings, which have been called the “ worst COP ever,” ended Sunday without an overarching agreement, after disputes over fossil fuels and climate finance pushed negotiations two days into overtime. With 2026 now expected to be one of the four hottest years in the climate record, the stakes of the summit were clear.

items.title: Overnight RSF drone attacks kill 19 in Sudan
items.summary: At least 19 people have been killed in drone attacks by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Sudan’s Blue Nile state, according to a rights group. A Sudanese military source told Al Jazeera that the RSF, which has been fighting Sudan’s army since 2023, targeted the city of Damazin in a series of attacks late on Tuesday that also wounded at least 20 people. The attacks targeted multiple sites across Damazin, the capital of Blue Nile, and the neighbouring town of Roseires. Three families were killed in the bombing of a residential area in Damazin, the military source said.

items.title: ASUS Turbo Radeon AI PRO R9700 Review
items.summary: While much of the attention in the market for AI inference has been focused on servers and datacenter-scale deployments, the heart and soul of the modern AI revolution started with video cards. And that is where it still beats on today, overshadowed by servers but still an important market segment overall. Within the AMD ecosystem, the company has taken a very visible pivot in how it markets and categorizes its professional video cards. The Radeon Pro lineup, once the backbone of AMD’s workstation graphics efforts, has become the Radeon AI Pro lineup, and the backbone of AMD’s add-in video card/AI accelerator efforts.

items.title: From Vulnerability Noise to Resilience: Rethinking Security in the AI Era
items.summary: AI-driven development is adding complexity to software supply chains, leaving security teams overwhelmed by vulnerabilities that may pose little actual risk. RapidFort explains how runtime visibility, container hardening, and automated remediation can reduce vulnerability noise and improve software resilience.

items.title: The biggest limitations of ChatGPT
items.summary: From fabricated citations to forgotten instructions, ChatGPT still has some frustrating blind spots. It's no secret that ChatGPT can write up emails, become your software troubleshooter and even dumb down complicated questions in an instant. But it's also pretty capable of making up responses so polished that you might not think to verify the shaky facts behind them. If only most of us had the confidence that ChatGPT has when it is hallucinating. Even after OpenAI brought its advanced GPT-6 model to all ChatGPT users in October 2026, the chatbot still has the tendency to fabricate supporting evidence, misread an ambiguous question and even forget instructions amid a lengthy conversation.

items.title: “I’m not going to remove the repository”
items.summary: There is a hacking tool called ARTEX that is causing havoc around the world. It lets a hacker plug in their LLM of choice, and ARTEX will then spin up a bunch of AI subagents focused on different aspects of hacking, such as scoping out a target or stealing data. This tool can complete an entire hack of a target in just a few hours. The original author of ARTEX took down the tool in October after it became clear that bad people were using it. But, as I write below, ARTEX is free. Several people are still distributing it on GitHub.
